summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University under Ryosaburo Sakaki and earned his doctorate from Kyoto University, where he served as professor and dean, later heading the Society for Near Eastern Studies.
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Otani University, where he served as lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

Atul Chandra Chatterjee was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University under Charles Henry Tawney, and later at King's College, Cambridge, serving in the Indian Civil Service from around 1897 to 1931.

August Blau specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under August Friedrich Pott and Carl Cappeller, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He held library posts at Wrocław, Göttingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he became librarian in 1892.

August Boeckh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).
August Clemens Schoener was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He pursued theology studies at the University of Munich and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1890 to 1894.

August Conrady worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, Jena, and Würzburg under Julius Jolly, completing his habilitation at Leipzig, where he became a professor and director, alongside a post at Peking University (1903–1904).
August Constantin Boltz was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena by 1845. He later served as a professor at the Prussian Military Academy from 1852 to 1864.

August Dillmann worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald, Rudolf von Roth, and August Schleicher, later holding professorships at Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and Frederick William University in Berlin.

August Ferdinand Naeke was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1805 to 1809 and held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Bonn (around 1818–1838).

August Fick specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Karl Friedrich Hermann, and Heinrich Ewald, later serving as an extraordinary professor at Göttingen and ordinary professor at the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Fischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and held posts at the University of Leipzig (around 1900–1930) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

August Friedrich Pott specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Karl Otfried Müller, Thomas Christian Tychsen, Franz Bopp, and Wilhelm von Humboldt, serving as professor of general linguistics at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and history. He studied at the Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he later taught as Privatdozent and professor for Tibetan.

August Hjalmar Edgren was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund University, the University of Gothenburg, and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

August Johan Bernet Kempers specialized in archaeology and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He directed Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional, Dinas Purbakala, and the Netherlands Open Air Museum, later teaching at the University of Amsterdam.
August Leskien was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as professor of Slavic philology at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

August Ludwig von Schlözer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University around 1758–1759 and held a post at the University of Göttingen from around 1769 to 1809.

August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others, holding professorships at Charles University, the German University in Prague, and the University of Jena.
August Sundin is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who is a PhD student at Ghent University (attested 2024 and 2026).
